My commitment to eliminating the Jedi is ''profound''. I am willing to give my life for that which grants me ''purpose''.|The Grand Inquisitor|[[Inquisitors 1|''Inquisitors'' 1]]}} '''The Grand Inquisitor''' was the title adopted by a [[Pau'an]] [[Gender|male]] [[Jedi Knight]] who turned to the [[dark side of the Force]] and became the [[Grand Inquisitor|leader]] of the [[Inquisitorius]], a band of [[Jedi hunter]]s who served the [[Galactic Empire]]. The Grand Inquisitor was once a [[Jedi Temple Guard]] and was involved in the events surrounding the [[Bombing of the Jedi Temple hangar|bombing]] of the [[Imperial Palace|Jedi Temple]] during the [[Clone Wars]], arresting the innocent and later exonerated [[Padawan]] [[Ahsoka Tano]] as well as the true culprit, [[Barriss Offee]]. After his fall to the dark side, the Grand Inquisitor was responsible for hunting down and [[Death|eliminating]] Jedi during the [[Great Jedi Purge]]. Selected by the [[Galactic Emperor|Emperor]], [[Darth Sidious]] himself, for the position of Grand Inquisitor, he personally served the [[Dark Lord of the Sith]], [[Anakin Skywalker|Darth Vader]], from whom he received his orders. Throughout his tenure he proved to be one of the regime's most proficient tools in eradicating the last of the [[Jedi Order]], being intimately familiar with the records of the Jedi Temple. The Grand Inquisitor took an active interest in eliminating the [[Spectres|rebel]] crew of the [[starship]] ''[[Ghost]]'', particularly the [[Jedi]] [[Kanan Jarrus]] and his Padawan, [[Ezra Bridger]]. He encountered these two Jedi on a number of occasions, including a [[Duel on Stygeon Prime]] and a [[Rescue of Tseebo|duel]] on the [[asteroid]] base [[Fort Anaxes]]. After the Grand Inquisitor and the government of [[Lothal]], from which the rebels operated, were consistently unable to eliminate the rebels, [[Grand Moff]] [[Wilhuff Tarkin]] arrived on Lothal to hunt for the rebels. Together, they [[Raid on the communications tower|captured]] Jarrus and hoped to use him to learn more about a larger rebel movement that was operating in the galaxy. They brought Jarrus to [[Mustafar]], where the rebels mounted a [[Action at Mustafar|rescue mission]] in [[orbit]]. During the operation, the Grand Inquisitor engaged Jarrus and Bridger in [[lightsaber combat]], and Jarrus eventually bested him. Rather than face the infamous wrath of [[Lord]] Vader for his repeated failures, the Grand Inquisitor chose to fall to his death. But despite the Inquisitor's physical death, Vader still had use for him. The [[Dark Lord of the Sith|Dark Lord]] was able to prevent the Inquisitor's spirit from passing on, instead tying it down to a [[Jedi outpost (Tempes)|Jedi outpost]] on [[Tempes]], where his spirit remained, killing all those who sought Jedi knowledge. After the Pau'an's death over Mustafar, the former [[Grand Master|Jedi Grand Master]] [[Yoda]] utilized a vision of the Grand Inquisitor as his former Jedi Temple Guard self to appear before Jarrus in the [[Lothal Jedi Temple|Jedi Temple]] on Lothal. In the vision, this '''Sentinel''' warned Jarrus that Bridger could fall to the dark side, and the two engaged in a lightsaber duel. After Jarrus refused to fight any further, the Sentinel knighted Jarrus and told him he was a Jedi Knight as the Grand Inquisitor once was. After losing [[Skywalker lightsaber|his lightsaber]] in [[3 ABY]], [[Luke Skywalker]] encountered the Inquisitor's spirit on Tempes. The two engaged in a duel that saw the young Skywalker come out victorious. As punishment for allowing the boy to escape, Vader refused the Pau'an's pleas to be set free from his prison, leaving him to guard the outpost for what the Inquisitor believed would be an eternity. ==Biography== ===Early life and knighthood=== {{Quote|The Grand Inquisitor. He had skills. He was ''trained'', at some point. Who is he?''"
"''A Jedi, once. Resentful that someone with his skill was not allowed access to the higher councils, the greater secrets of the Order.|Darth Vader and Darth Sidious|}} [[File:Sentinel.png|thumb|left|250px|The Grand Inquisitor was originally a Jedi Knight and a guardian of the sacred Jedi Temple on Coruscant.]] A long-lived [[Pau'an]]{{Asmodee|subdomain=shop|url=star-wars-5-shatterpoint-jedi-hunters-swp12|text=Star Wars: Shatterpoint - Jedi Hunters}} [[Gender|male]] who would one [[Standard day|day]] become the [[Grand Inquisitor]], the Force-sensitive Pau'an [[Homeworld|hailed]] from the [[planet]] [[Utapau]]. At some point, he became a member of the [[Jedi Order]] and rose to the rank of [[Jedi Knight]]. As a [[Jedi]], he served in the [[Jedi Temple Guard]], a group of Jedi tasked with defending the [[Imperial Palace|Jedi Temple]] on [[Coruscant]].{{TCW|The Wrong Jedi}} During his time as a Jedi Knight, the Jedi proved himself a skilled individual. The knight eventually developed a hatred [[Jedi Code|unbecoming of a Jedi]], for [[Chief Librarian]] [[Jocasta Nu]]; Despite his level of skill, the Jedi was annoyed with the repressiveness of the Order, being denied access to the deeper secrets of the Force, particularly the dark side. When he would go to the [[Jedi Archives]] as he served the order, he was denied access by the elder Jedi most of the time. When he was allowed to read some [[datafile]]s on occasions, he was watched closely by her, as she deemed him as unfit for education.[[Darth Vader (2017) 7|''Darth Vader'' (2017) 7]] ===Trial of Ahsoka Tano=== [[File:BarrissInCourt-TWJ.png|thumb|right|300px|The future Grand Inquisitor was one of the Jedi Temple Guards who brought Barriss Offee before Supreme Chancellor Sheev Palpatine.]] During the [[Clone Wars]], in a period of protests against the [[Jedi High Council]] for their continued leadership over the war between the [[Galactic Republic]] and the [[Confederacy of Independent Systems]], a [[Bombing of the Jedi Temple hangar|bombing]] at the Jedi Temple rocked the Jedi Order.{{TCW|Sabotage (episode)}} Although the true culprit was [[Padawan]] [[Barriss Offee]], who believed that the Jedi Order had lost its way and were the true villains in the war against the Confederacy, she framed her friend and fellow Padawan [[Ahsoka Tano]] for the crime. Tano fled into the [[Coruscant Underworld]], away from the [[Grand Army of the Republic]] forces that pursued her, but she was eventually captured and brought to the Jedi Temple. She was brought before the Jedi Council, who stripped her of her Padawan status and expelled her from the Jedi Order. The future Grand Inquisitor was one of the guardsmen who led Tano from the Jedi Temple,{{WebCite|url=https://www.forbes.com/sites/lukethompson/2016/03/29/review-star-wars-rebels-season-finale-non-spoiler-and-the-inquisitors-past-revealed|text=Reaction: 'Star Wars Rebels' Season Finale [Non-Spoiler], And The Inquisitor's Past Revealed|author=Thompson, Luke Y.|work=[[Wikipedia:Forbes|Forbes]]|archivedate=20200131114328}} and she was ultimately brought to [[Trial of Ahsoka Tano|trial]] before [[Supreme Chancellor]] [[Darth Sidious|Palpatine]]. During the trial, Tano's master, Jedi Knight [[Anakin Skywalker]], [[Duel at the Jedi Temple|uncovered]] Offee's duplicity and had her arrested. The future Grand Inquisitor was one of the guards who escorted Offee into the trial,''[[Ultimate Star Wars, New Edition]]'' where she admitted her guilt in front of the chancellor and was subsequently taken away by the guards. Tano was exonerated, but she refused to rejoin the Jedi Order and chose to seek a new path.{{Databank|ahsoka-tano|Ahsoka Tano}} ===Fall to the dark side=== {{Quote|You do know the Emperor ''personally'' selected me, Vader? Raised me up, gave me this position. He ''believes'' in my ability.|The Grand Inquisitor, to Darth Vader|}} [[File:Swi30_preview.jpg|thumb|left|250px|The former Jedi Temple Guard became an Inquisitor after turning to the dark side of the Force.]] The events with Offee and Tano left the future Grand Inquisitor feeling disaffected, and he lost faith in the Jedi Order. This left him susceptible to the pull of the [[Dark side of the Force|dark side]] of [[the Force]], and ultimately fell to the dark side. However, the Pau'an was still a Jedi by the time the Clone Wars ended, as he was a survivor of [[Order 66]]. At the end of the war, the Supreme Chancellor—secretly the [[Dark Lord of the Sith]] [[Darth]] Sidious—[[Proclamation of the New Order|transformed]] the Republic into the [[Galactic Empire]] and declared himself [[Galactic Emperor|Emperor]] of [[the galaxy]].{{Film|III}} During this time, the [[Emperor]] recruited him to become Grand Inquisitor of the [[Inquisitorius]] when he promised the Jedi Knight the chance to read through the secrets of the Jedi Archives.''[[Star Wars: The Dark Side]]'' As Grand Inquisitor, he led other members of the Inquisitorius. Among these Inquisitors were dark warriors such as the [[Second Sister]], the [[Fifth Brother]],{{Rebels|Always Two There Are}} the [[Sixth Brother]],[[Ahsoka (novel)|''Ahsoka'']] the [[Seventh Sister]], the [[Eighth Brother]],{{Rebels|Twilight of the Apprentice}} the [[Ninth Sister]], and the [[Tenth Brother]].[[Darth Vader (2017) 14|''Darth Vader'' (2017) 14]] Like the Grand Inquisitor, these Inquisitors had their roots in the Jedi Order. ===Servant of an empire=== ====Serving Lord Vader==== {{Quote|Your task is to search the Archives for clues as to where surviving Jedi might be now. Personal information…family connections. Anything. Do not delay. Do not allow yourself to become distracted. Do not ''fail''.''"
"''Don't worry, Vader. I've waited my whole life for this.|Darth Vader and the Grand Inquisitor|}} [[File:VaderVSGrandInquisitor-2017DarthVader6.png|thumb|right|250px|Not knowing each other, the Grand Inquisitor briefly dueled with his future master.]] Though the Inquisitor came into the service of the Empire and the [[Sith]], he was not a Sith himself. When the Inquisitor entered the Jedi Temple's Archives, he was [[Duel in the former Jedi Temple|confronted]] by the [[Sith Lord]] [[Darth]] Vader, who was once Anakin Skywalker before his own fall to the dark side. He and the [[cyborg]] then fought each other until the latter damaged his [[The Grand Inquisitor's lightsaber|lightsaber]]. The fight was then stopped by the Emperor, who explained to [[Lord]] Vader who the Inquisitor and the Inquisitorius were. They then went to the [[Inquisitorius Headquarters]] in [[The Works]], where the Grand Inquisitor introduced Vader to the other Inquisitors as their new master. Vader then tasked the Inquisitor with hunting down and eliminating any Jedi who had survived Order 66, the order given to the [[clone trooper]]s of the Grand Army of the Republic to destroy the Jedi Order. To accomplish this task, the Inquisitor was trained in the ways of the dark side and studied the records of the Jedi Temple in order to better know his enemies.{{Rebels|Rise of the Old Masters}} Seeing how his new master employed brutal training methods that resulted in the loss of limbs from various of his Inquisitors, the Grand Inquisitor questioned Vader's methods, but the Sith Lord responded by saying that he was teaching loss to the Inquisitors and that they still fought like Jedi. After some arguing, The Grand Inquisitor reminded Vader the if the Inquisitors were to fail, said failure would be reflected on him as the Emperor appointed him to train them. As he and his master arrived at the former Jedi Temple, the Grand Inquisitor confided in Lord Vader about his hatred for Jedi Master Jocasta Nu as she denied him full access to the Jedi Archives. Now with a high ranking position at the Empire, the Grand Inquisitor claimed that he would read through everything in the Jedi Archives. Vader then assigned him to track down of any remaining Jedi survivors, a task the Inquisitor assured his master that he would not fail. ====Hunting Jocasta Nu==== {{Quote|I used to dream of this, you know. Striking you down. I thought it would be so ''easy''. After all, they didn't stick you in the library because of your ''combat skills''. Before the Purge, I could never find a way to do it—the other Jedi would have stopped me. But now…there ''are'' no other Jedi.|The Grand Inquisitor, whilst dueling Jocasta Nu|[[Darth Vader (2017) 9|''Darth Vader'' (2017) 9]]}} Unbeknownst to the Inquisitor, Jocasta Nu had infiltrated the Jedi Temple in hopes of retrieving a holocron with a list of every Force-sensitive child catalogued prior to Order 66. While the Inquisitor was unaware of Nu's presence, as he was poring over the Jedi archives, the Jedi Master soon revealed herself to him, claiming that he had no right to read her books nor toss them aside.[[Darth Vader (2017) 8|''Darth Vader'' (2017) 8]] [[File:DarthVaderSavesJocastaNu-2017DarthVader9.png|thumb|left|250px|Despite defeating Jocasta Nu, the Inquisitor was prevented from killing her by Vader.]] Held at bladepoint, The Grand Inquisitor soon revealed to Nu that he was once a Jedi who she denied access to her books even when they were on the same side, though the Inquisitor soon whipped out his own lightsaber and started a duel with the Jedi Master. During their brief duel, the Grand Inquisitor explained to Nu why he left the Jedi Order and told her that he had dreamed of striking her down for a long time. The Grand Inquisitor gained the upper hand during the duel and defeated Nu by knocking her to the ground, but he was prevented from killing the Jedi Master by Darth Vader, who claimed that he did not wish for her to be executed; in reality Vader was carrying the Emperor's orders of not to share information about Master Nu's importance. While the two argued, Nu took advantage of their distraction to hurl several holobooks at her opponents with the Force, which knocked the Grand Inquisitor unconscious. Vader eventually carried the hunt for Nu and killed her.[[Darth Vader (2017) 10|''Darth Vader'' (2017) 10]] At some point, the Grand Inquisitor assigned the [[Fifth Brother]] the task of killing his first Jedi. The Inquisitor succeeded without flaw, providing him a sense of validation.''[[Star Wars Jedi: Battle Scars]]'' ====Acquainting Akaris==== {{Quote|Here among the Inquisitorius, you will whet your skills against those of your brothers and sisters. You will seek the answers that have been kept from you, study the darkest depths of what the Force can do. You will learn that you can only harness your truest strength when you fully embrace your power and don't hold back. Even now, you didn't fully commit, but that Jedi reticence won't last long. If you don't rise to my expectations…well, you won't survive long enough to worry.''"
"''Who are you?''"
"''I'm the Grand Inquisitor, and for the foreseeable future, I'm the one you will want to impress.|The Grand Inquisitor and Iskat Akaris|}} [[File:IskatAkaris.jpg|thumb|right|300px|Iskar Akaris would soon join the Inquisitorius as the Thirteenth Sister]] On Coruscant, the Grand Inquisitor was brought the [[Pkorian]] [[Thirteenth Sister|Iskat Akaris]] by clone troopers aboard a shuttle. Presenting Akaris her lightsabers, the Inquisitor asked the former Jedi whether she was ready to abandon her past in favor of a future of her own making, to which she agreed. The Inquisitor welcomed Akaris to the Inquisitorius and drew his own saber as a challenge. Circling Akaris, he parried her strikes easily, toying with and verbally mocking her. Akaris questioned the nature of the Inquisitorius and, as the Grand Inquisitor began to explain, shoved the Pau'an back with the Force. The Inquisitor discarded his cape and informed her that the Jedi were almost extinct, recounting [[Mace Windu]]'s attempt on Chancellor Palpatine's life and Order 66. The Pkorian wondered aloud how the Inquisitor knew about her and the truth about her mother, knowledge the Inquisitor taunted his opponent with, claiming that Akaris had to earn it. Akaris switched to a technique she had learned from [[Kelleran Beq]], which the Inquisitor blocked before disengaging. Deactivating his weapon, the Inquisitor declared that Akaris' performance was sufficient and properly introduced himself. Akaris hurled her first lightsaber at him, causing the Inquisitor to destroy it and bind Akaris in place with the Force, reminding her that she had much to learn before letting her go and walking away. ====Mission to Bar'leth==== {{Quote|If you wish this Gamodar to remain alive, you will convince him to open his safe. If not, I will destroy him and take what I wish.''"
"''I understand, Grand Inquisitor.''"
"''Impress me, and things will go well. Disappoint me at your peril.|The Grand Inquisitor and Iskat Akaris|}} Some time later, the Grand Inquisitor approached Akaris while she was performing calisthenics and, leading her to a landing pad, informed her of an assignment to visit [[Gamodar]], an [[Ortolan]] trader she had visited on [[Bar'leth]] alongside her Jedi Master, Sember Vey, in search of relics. Boarding the [[Scythe (Phi-class)|''Scythe'']], a [[Phi-class shuttle|''Phi''-class shuttle]],''[[Star Wars: Dawn of Rebellion: The Visual Guide]]'' the pair set off at once. The Grand Inquisitor piloted the ship, making it clear by his demeanor that he did not wish to be disturbed. Upon arrival, Akaris questioned whether their task was a common one for the Inquisitorius, to which the Inquisitor replied that the organization itself was uncommon, tasked with taking possession of what once belonged to the Jedi. [[File:Unlimited-GrandInquisitor.png|thumb|left|300px|The Grand Inquisitor]] The Inquisitor set down at Gamodar's shop and inquired about the trader. Akaris, though reluctant, relayed what she knew, including Gamodar's security measures and the likely location of his relics within a safe. The Grand Inquisitor instructed Akaris to convince to open the safe, threatening to end the Ortolan's life should she disappoint him and departing the ship. Gamodar happily reunited with Akaris. When the shop keeper, unfamiliar with the Inquisitors, asked whether they were keepers of the peace, the Grand Inquisitor indicated that the answer was circumstantial, prompting Akaris to directly ask Gamodar for the artifacts that the duo sought. Gamodar relented and returned to his shop, only to release his security droid, Lump, on his guests. Akaris destroyed it with her lightsaber, and the Grand Inquisitor ordered her to retrieve the relics or die alongside the Ortolan as well. The Inquisitor waited and, after Akaris ultimately murdered Gamodar, was pleased when she returned with a red, triangular holocron, revealing it to be the item that he had sought specifically. The Inquisitor told Akaris to bring the rest before striding back to the ship, which she did. Upon their return to Coruscant, the Grand Inquisitor led Akaris into a chamber within Inquisitorius Headquarters where she was officially inducted into the Inquisitorius; Akaris swore allegiance to the Inquisitor and his masters and received the title Thirteenth Sister, though she did not yet wish to use it. ====Akaris' independence==== {{Quote|News has reached us of two rogue Jedi hiding on Firrhana. You will travel to the Outer Rim, root them out, and destroy them. Do you understand?''"
"''Yes, Grand Inquisitor.''"
"''Look at me child. This is your first real mission. It is one thing to realize that the Jedi are the enemy, but it is another thing entirely to participate in their necessary eradication. Do not give them a chance to speak, to poison you with their rhetoric, for they will attempt to sway you with their weak persuasion and pathetic mewling. You are a Jedi no longer.|The Grand Inquisitor and Iskat Akaris|}} [[File:Camtono.jpg|thumb|right|245px|Iskat Akaris retuned with a camtono (a camtono pictured).]] Subsequent to the mission to Bar'leth, the Grand Inquisitor halted a duel between Akaris and the Seventh Sister. The Inquisitor summoned Akaris after she returned from an expedition of self-discovery to her homeworld of Pkori, to ask what she had learned. Akaris relayed the truth of her past, which the Grand Inquisitor expressed it was foolish of the Jedi to keep from her. The Pau'an inquired as to the nature of the [[camtono]] Akaris had brought with her, supposing it to be another relic. Akaris informed him that the device, which she had acquired the device from Morgest, another of Vey's associates, on Takodana, did contain an artifact—a lightsaber. The Grand Inquisitor summoned the weapon to his hand, inspected it, and praised Akaris for returning with a boon to diminish the waste of his time before dismissing her. The Grand Inquisitor sent for Akaris again after a lightsaber wound from her former friend and fellow Inquisitor [[Tualon Yaluna]] landed her in the medbay for the third time, the [[RA-7 protocol droid]] [[6-RA-7]] instructing the Pkorian to report to the Grand Inquisitor's chambers. There, he sat upon his throne and asked Akaris whether she was recovered from her latest injury. Akaris shortly confirmed that she had, having learned that that was the only right answer. The Inquisitor then gave Akaris her first true mission, to investigate and destroy two rogue Jedi on the Outer Rim world of [[Firrhana]], and warned her not to be swayed by her enemies' words, rhetoric he considered to be "weak persuasion" and "pathetic mewling." Akaris inquired as to the names of the Jedi, which the Inquisitor dismissed as unimportant, as they were all traitors. The Inquisitor then sent her on her way, Akaris promising not disappoint him. The Grand Inquisitor awaited Akaris in his chambers alongside Darth Vader. Akaris returned, and the Inquisitor inquired as to the Pkorian's success, which she affirmed by placing three lightsabers before him. Vader praised Akaris, to which she rejected the name, embracing her new identity as the Thirteenth Sister. ====An evaluation on Nur==== {{Quote|I must confess, you've impressed us. You both have. Unfortunately, there is only room in our ranks for one. And so, you must face one final test.''"
''''[The Grand Inquisitor produces a lightsaber]''''
"''You may choose not to fight, of course. In which case, both of you will die.|The Grand Inquisitor, to Barriss Offee and Dante|{{TOTE|Devoted}}}} On Nur, the Grand Inquisitor introduced himself to [[Ahmar]], [[Dante]], and [[Barriss Offee]], three former Jedi brought before him by [[Fourth Sister]], at [[Fortress Inquisitorius]]. Questioned by Offee, he informed them of fall of the Jedi and the reorganization of the Republic into the first Galactic Empire. Citing the need for order, the Inquisitor informed the trio that the prospect of protecting the Emperor's vision lay before them before sending the Jedi to their quarters and advising them not to leave. [[File:Devoted-TotE.png|thumb|left|250px|Barriss Offee trained with the Grand Inquisitor, who administered her final test.]] Ahmar later tried to escape. Dante and Offee were subsequently brought before the Inquisitor, who informed them that their companion had suffered an "accident" and, after dismissing the Fourth Sister and Dante, took Offee aside to train. Proceeding to a hidden chamber, the Grand Inquisitor lectured Offee on the limitations of her Jedi training and presented her with a lightsaber. Instructing Offee to attack him, the Inquisitor easily evaded her strikes. The Pau'an told Offee to embrace her anger, leading her to strike him. The Inquisitor then praised Offee before retaliating, calling upon the Force to violently throw his opponent against the ceiling. Further goading caused Offee to push the Inquisitor into a wall in retaliation, bloodying the Pau'an and earning a smirk. The Grand Inquisitor, impressed with both Dante and Offee, oversaw a final duel between the pair. Offee, initially reluctant to fight, strangled her opponent to death with the Force, earning her a place amongst the Inquisitorius. The Pau'an was later present alongside Fourth Sister, Offee, [[Marrok|First Brother]], and the [[Eleventh Brother]] for the arrival of Darth Vader. The Inquisitors knelt before their master until the Grand Inquisitor rose and ordered the others to stand as well, proclaiming the phrase "[[long live the Empire]]." ====Later missions==== {{Quote|Kira Vantala. I admit that I'm surprised. Of all those who might have survived the purge…I did not imagine a weakling such as you to be among them.''"
"''Then that was your mistake, for the dark side has forever underestimated me.|The Grand Inquisitor and Kira Vantala|{{StoryCite|story=The Orphanage (short story)|book=Dark Legends}}}} At some stage, the Grand Inquisitor would also trained [[Reva Sevander|Third Sister]], improving both her skills in [[Jar'Kai]] and teaching her a aggressive version of his preferred [[Form II]].{{AtomicMassGames|url=transmission/databank-download-grand-inquisitor-fallen-jedi-third-sister-preview|text=Databank Download: Grand Inquisitor, Fallen Jedi & Third Sister Preview}} However, he maintained a low opinion of her abilities. At one point during his service to the Empire, the Inquisitor embarked on a quest for answers that involved him tracking down a bearded human. As the man hid, the Inquisitor pursued with his lightsaber ignited.{{FFGTCG|set=Promise of Power|cardname=Press for Answers|link=alliances-cycle/promise-of-power/press-for-answers-r2114}} [[File:TheOrphanage.jpg|thumb|right|240px|The Grand Inquisitor abducted children from an orphanage on Gaaten.]] One Jedi that the Inquisitor led to their [[death]] was [[Jedi Master]] [[Luminara Unduli]]. After the execution of Order 66, Unduli was captured and held in the [[Spire (Stygeon Prime)|Spire]], a former Separatist[[Darth Maul — Son of Dathomir 1|''Darth Maul — Son of Dathomir'' 1]]-turned-Imperial [[prison]] on [[Stygeon Prime]]. At her end, Unduli was in the presence of the Inquisitor, who stood in the doorway of her cell as she walked into an execution chamber and died. The Inquisitor kept her remains in the prison cell, using them to lure other Jedi to their deaths when they heard rumors that Unduli was still alive. A [[Hologram|holographic]] recording of Unduli and her execution was kept by the Empire as part of this ruse. As the Grand Inquisitor, the dark side adept hunted down and dueled the former Jedi Padawan [[Naq Med]]. His lightsaber was damaged in the duel and Med escaped.''[[Force Collector]]'' At another point, the Grand Inquisitor took Force-sensitive children from an [[Gaaten orphanage|orphanage]] on [[Gaaten]]. One night when he went to the orphanage, he was confronted by a surviving Jedi, [[Kira Vantala]], to which the Grand Inquisitor expressed his shock, believing her to be a weak Jedi. The Inquisitor was defeated by Vantala and a [[refugee]] named [[Elish]], and never returned to the orphanage. ====Evidence of another survivor==== {{Quote|Set a course back to base. And inform Lord Vader that we have found evidence of another survivor.|The Grand Inquisitor, after investigating the Sixth Brother's death on Raada|}} [[File:DV16Cover-SixthBrother.jpg|thumb|left|240px|The Grand Inquisitor investigated the death of the Sixth Brother and realized it confirmed another survivor of the Great Jedi Purge.]] One [[Standard year|year]] after the rise of the Galactic Empire, the Grand Inquisitor was alerted of the presence of a [[Force-sensitive]] being old enough to have received [[Jedi training]] on the [[farm]]ing [[moon]] of [[Raada]]. Though he wanted to hunt down the supposed Jedi himself, he was needed elsewhere, and the task instead went to the Sixth Brother, who then went to Raada to lay a trap for the Force-sensitive. However, he was killed in the following [[Raada Uprising|battle]], and the Jedi, as well as the [[farmer]]s who had rebelled against the recent occupation, escaped. Meanwhile, the Grand Inquisitor was alerted to the situation and traveled to the moon with a [[fleet]] of [[Imperial-class Star Destroyer|Star Destroyers]] to provide backup, but by the time they arrived, the insurgents were gone. The Grand Inquisitor personally examined the damage done by the battle and discovered the corpse of the Sixth Brother. Though annoyed by the incompetence and recklessness of his subordinate, the Grand Inquisitor was impressed by what the Jedi had done. He then went back to his ship and instructed his [[agent]]s to set a course back to base and to inform Lord Vader that they had found evidence of another survivor—who was, in fact, Ahsoka Tano, Anakin Skywalker's former Padawan. ====The rogue Inquisitors==== {{Quote|We know they're out there, but there have been no signs, no signals. For all intents and purposes, they have vanished.|The Grand Inquisitor, to Darth Vader|[[Darth Vader (2017) 19|''Darth Vader'' (2017) 19]]}} In [[14 BBY]],''[[Star Wars: Timelines]]'' Lord Vader took the Fifth Brother,[[Darth Vader (2017) 19|''Darth Vader'' (2017) 19]] the [[Thirteenth Sister]], and [[Tualon Yaluna]]''[[Inquisitor: Rise of the Red Blade]]'' to hunt the former Jedi Master and Council member [[Eeth Koth]]. The mission was a success as they not only managed to kill the Jedi Master but to kidnap his force-sensitive daughter. As his master arrived at The Works, the Grand Inquisitor congratulated Vader for capturing a child that would be used as part of Project Harvester. After they gave Koth's child to two masked red figures, the Inquisitor led Vader away and showed him a list of surviving Jedi that included [[Yoda]], [[Obi-Wan Kenobi]], [[Coleman Kcaj]], [[Oppo Rancisis]], [[Selrahc Eluos]], and [[Ka-Moon Kholi]] on a holoprojector. The Inquisitor told Vader that a Jedi would slip up eventually, they just had to wait. [[File:HiddenExtremelyWell-2017DarthVader19.jpg|230px|thumb|The Inquisitor shows Vader a list of Jedi Purge survivors.]] The Grand Inquisitor was at a cantina with his fellow Inquisitors when Lord Vader arrived and attacked two of the Inquisitors that had previously helped him during his hunt for Koth. The Grand Inquisitor[[Darth Vader (2017) 20|''Darth Vader'' (2017) 20]] cautiously asked Vader if this sudden attack was a test or more training, to which the Sith Lord replied that it was not before continuing his attacks on the two Inquisitors that ended up escaping from the headquarters. The Grand Inquisitor asked his master if he and the other Inquisitors could assist him in any way, but Lord Vader declined his offer and [[Coruscant Incident|chased]] the rogue Inquisitors by himself before killing both of them. Unfortunately, the Dark Lord's chase resulted in the death of [[Maklooq]], a Gran Senator that was important to the Emperor's plans; this resulted in the Inquisitorius being moved to Fortress Inquisitorius on Nur as Sidious wanted to maintain the organization's clandestine nature. ====Kashyyyk and the Shroud==== {{Quote|This technology holds infinite potential.''"
"''Including helping us to eradicate the remaining Jedi forever.''"
"''Yes. The remaining straggling Jedi in the galaxy will fall, once the Shroud is in our hands. Are you capable of this task, Fifth Brother?''"
"''I am capable. ''[…]''''"
"''Then go. I shall await your triumph.|The Grand Inquisitor and Fifth Brother|}} Later that year,''[[Star Wars: Timelines]]'' dates the events of ''[[Star Wars Jedi: Fallen Order]]'' to [[14 BBY]]. the Grand Inquisitor heard about a Jedi who caused problems for the Empire on [[Kashyyyk]]. This Jedi was [[Cal Kestis]], who helped the [[Partisans]] to [[Liberation on Kashyyyk|attack]] an [[Imperial Refinery]]. The Ninth Sister told the Grand Inquisitor that Kestis would not be someone stupid enough to return to Kashyyyk, especially after the [[Kashyyyk resistance|resistance]] was eliminated by the Empire. The Ninth Sister was later proved wrong and defeated by Kestis when he returned to Kashyyyk.''[[Star Wars Jedi: Fallen Order]]'' Years after that, the Grand Inquisitor communicated with the Fifth Brother via hologram, the latter aboard his starship. As the Fifth Brother knelt before his superior, the Pau'an assigned him to find the [[Shroud]], a personal cloaking shield created by the [[Kadas'sa'Nikto]] [[Irei]]. The Grand Inquisitor confirmed that the technology would at last destroy the Jedi before questioning his subordinate's ability to resolve the assignment. Confident, the Fifth Brother affirmed his commitment, and the Grand Inquisitor dismissed him. The Fifth Brother was ultimately foiled by Kestis. ===Tensu Run must die=== ====Diagu and the ''Devastator''==== {{Quote|The Diagu are Jedi sympathizers. Credible intelligence has Tensu Run building a refuge here. Reveal his whereabouts or every last Diagu will meet the same fate as your late elder.|The Grand Inquisitor|}} Darth Vader ordered the Grand Inquisitor to bring him the head of the legendary Jedi [[Tensu Run]]. Traveling aboard the ''Scythe'', the Inquisitor arrived on [[Targyon]] in pursuit of Run, a mission he believed might require him to sacrifice his life. Accompanied by Purge troopers, the Inquisitor approached a [[Diagu]] village elder and asked for Run's whereabouts, to which the elder simply answered that Run was not there. The elder claimed that anyone hunting Run would come to despair, though the Inquisitor countered that Run brought despair everywhere he went. The Grand Inquisitor then executed the elder and instructed the local people to reveal where Run was hiding or meet the same fate. When no one offered any information, the Inquisitor ordered the children separated and condemned their parents for their willingness to leave the younglings orphaned for nothing in return. The Inquisitor promised a child that the Empire would not abandon them, but was unable to leave them unharmed. One of the villagers stepped forward and told the Grand Inquisitor that Tensu Run had been heading toward Targyon's fourth moon. The Pau'an revealed that the moon had been scanned upon approach and that Run was not there. Ordering the children taken to Coruscant and the rest of the crowd executed, the Inquisitor boarded his ship and reflected that Run had become an idea and therefore much more difficult to kill, but that he still intended to locate him. Aboard the ''Devastator'', the Inquisitor reported to Darth Vader, who was disappointed with his progress. The Inquisitor cited the willingness of the people to defend Run, who Vader declared had become a symbol of hope. Vader recounted the conquest of Regis Kor, the raid on an Imperial outpost that made Run famous, instructing the Inquisitorius to search the far reaches of the galaxy for the fugitive. Vader asked whether the Grand Inquisitor recalled the satisfaction of joining the dark side, which he did, explaining that Run made others feel the same way and therefore must die. ====Inquisitions and aberrations==== {{Quote|There are beautiful places in the galaxy. They are an aberration. The majority of existence requires authority. It requires order. And to bring order to this galaxy…Tensu Run must die.|The Grand Inquisitor|}} On [[Gerrenthum]], the Inquisitor interrogated a [[Gamorrean]] who could not understand him before receiving a tip from an alien cargo salvager. Tracking Run to the Jedi cruiser ''Voyager Dawn'', the Grand Inquisitor ordered the ''Scythe''{{'s}} Purge trooper crew to destroy the enemy's defense ships and disable the ''Dawn''{{'s}} navigation systems. Boarding the ''Dawn'', the Inquisitor confronted Jedi Master [[Elan Rast]] and, striking down the Master's medical droid, inquired about Run's presence. Rast told the Inquisitor that Run had been there and smiled, viewing their inevitable death as a mercy. The Inquisitor questioned Rast's demeanor provided the impending execution of the other Jedi aboard. As the Pau'an ignited his lightsaber, the Master stated that the Inquisitor was once a good man and was therefore aware of Rast's feelings, which the Inquisitor confirmed. The Inquisitor questioned the remaining Jedi about Run's whereabouts before promptly slaughtering them. He then considered, as he had whilst in transit to Targyon, that places of beauty were aberrations in a galaxy that required order. For that reason, the Inquisitor settled on the necessity of Run's demise. The Grand Inquisitor met with Vader again at his fortress on Mustafar. The Pau'an explained the complications brought about by support amongst Run's believers and his attempt to weaken Run's resolve by killing his master. Vader deemed the Inquisitor's strategy sufficient, though warned him that failure would lead to suffering for the Inquisitors.[[Inquisitors 2|''Inquisitors'' 2]] ====Where you are==== {{Quote|Do you forget the ''peace'' that once flowed within you? A life free of tormented lust for ''power?''''"
"''Do you forget the euphoria? The raw desire that coursed through your veins? You of all people should know it matters more where we are than where we've been.''"
''''[Darth Vader tosses Run]''''
"''The Jedi Code has brought you here, Tensu Run. This is where you are.''"
"''Like a relic of a dying faith, you will be forgotten.|Tensu Run, the Grand Inquisitor, and Darth Vader|[[Inquisitors 4|''Inquisitors'' 4]]}} On the ''Devastator'', Darth Vader once more instructed the Inquisitors, including the Grand Inquisitor, to kill Tensu Run, threatening deadly consequences should they fail. Vader and the Inquisitors did so successfully. ===The Kenobi ordeal=== ====A rat in the desert==== {{Quote|In actuality, I would say the Jedi hunt themselves. Do you know the key to hunting a Jedi, friend? It is patience. Jedi cannot help what they are. Their compassion leaves a trail. For example, in our line of work, rumors run rampant. Here's one I heard just recently. It involves a Jedi hiding right here in your lovely saloon. Let's say ours is a wanderer. Maybe he's looking for people like him. Comes across this establishment. Nice place. And then he sees you. A man in need. Perhaps the locals are stealing from you. Threatening you. So what is the Jedi to do? Help you and risk exposure? Or move on? Now, if he were smart, he'd keep moving, but the Jedi Code is like an itch. He cannot help it. So he steps in and saves your saloon. You offer him a place to hide. Fresh water, shade from the suns, but the stories, they begin and they travel quickly. His compassion has been his undoing.|The Grand Inquisitor to a saloon owner|}} [[File:GrandInquisitorBarkeepConvo-OWKp1.png|thumb|left|250px|The Grand Inquisitor interrogated a bartender regarding the whereabouts of a Jedi on Tatooine.]] In [[9 BBY]],{{KenobiDate|I}} the Grand Inquisitor [[Search for Nari|traveled]] to [[Tatooine]] with the Fifth Brother and the [[Reva Sevander|Third Sister]]. They soon landed in [[Mos Eisley]] and the three Inquisitorius began to seek out a Jedi they were hunting. The Grand Inquisitor and his fellow Inquisitorius walked into a saloon and asked the [[Unidentified saloon owner|establishment's owner]] if he knew who they were and what they did. The owner recognized them as Inquisitors and that they hunted Jedi, leading the Grand Inquisitor to express his point of view that actually the Jedi are the ones who "hunt themselves down," since they left a trail of compassion. He went on to inform the saloon's owner that the Inquisitorius had heard rumors about a Jedi hiding in the saloon, musing if that Jedi had come there to help with the owner's tensions with the locals in exchange for food and shelter. Just as the Grand Inquisitor began to conclude his speech, the Third Sister got tired of waiting and threw a patron's knife towards the saloon's owner. This made [[Nari]], the Jedi they were seeking out, save him with the Force. Discovered, Nari tried to run away, but the Third Sister and the Fifth Brother cornered him. As the Grand Inquisitor ordered the Inquisitorius to prepare Nari for interrogation, the Third Sister tried to cut the Jedi down, leading the Inquisitor to stop and knock the Sister aside with the Force, enabling him to escape. As the Fifth Brother pursued Nari, the Grand Inquisitor reprimanded the Third Sister for her carelessness, warning her that if she didn't quit her fixation with finding Obi-Wan Kenobi—whom she deemed a bigger prey than "scraps" like Nari—she would be relieved of her duties. As the Grand Inquisitor strode off into the desert, the Third Sister retorted that she considered Kenobi forgotten. ====Third Sister's gambit==== {{Quote|Third Sister! I can stand the reek of your ambition no longer.''"
"''I found him. We have him!''"
"''And I cannot risk you losing him again. Move aside.|The Grand Inquisitor and Third Sister|{{Kenobi|Part II}}}} [[File:Grand_Inquisitor_on_Daiyu.jpg|thumb|right|250px|The Grand Inquisitor interrogated Vect Nokru on Daiyu.]] After the Third Sister hired [[Vect Nokru]] and his [[Mercenary|mercenaries]] to [[Ambush on Alderaan|kidnap]] the [[Alderaanian]] [[Princess]] [[Leia Skywalker Organa Solo|Leia Organa]] and bring her to [[Daiyu]] in hopes that Obi-Wan Kenobi would be contacted by Leia's adoptive father, [[Bail Prestor Organa|Bail Organa]], to rescue her, the Grand Inquisitor went to Daiyu accompanied by the Fifth Brother and the [[Fourth Sister]] so they could [[Hunt for Obi-Wan|capture]] Kenobi. They met up with the Third Sister, and the Inquisitor chastised her for kidnapping a [[senator]]'s daughter and for not informing him. Feeling that the Third Sister wanted to capture Kenobi to gain favor within the Inquisitorius ranks, the Grand Inquisitor reminded her how they rescued her from the "gutter" and that she would always be the "least" of them, leading the Sister to insult him. Unamused, the Inquisitor asked the Fifth Brother to secure the city and informed the Third Sister of his intentions to deliver Kenobi himself, dismissing her from the hunt by saying that she was no longer required and that he would deal with her once he returned from hunting Kenobi. [[File:Third_Sister_stabs_the_Grand_Inquisitor.jpg|thumb|left|250px|During their mission on Daiyu, The Grand Inquisitor was betrayed by the Third Sister.]] As they secured the city, the Grand Inquisitor requested the Fifth Brother to shut down the planet's port and request a [[garrison]] within an [[Standard hour|hour]]. The Fourth Sister then came to him and showed him a bounty hunter alert advertising a [[bounty]] placed on Kenobi's head, leading the Grand Inquisitor to deduce that the Third Sister had once again acted behind his back. Soon afterward, two stormtroopers brought Nokru to his presence, and the Grand Inquisitor activated his lightsaber to threaten Nokru if he didn't tell him where Kenobi was, knowing that he had put the bounty on Third Sister's behalf. However, Nokru knew nothing, leading the Inquisitor to kill him for his uselessness. Not long after, the Grand Inquisitor intercepted the Third Sister as she taunted Kenobi, wishing him to come out from where he was hiding so she could deliver him personally to Lord Vader. The Inquisitor stated that he would not tolerate the "reek" of her ambition any longer and ordered her to move aside, not wanting to lose Kenobi again, thanks to the Third Sister's recklessness. He then instructed her to watch and learn as he used the Force to move aside the crates which Kenobi was using to hide, but the Third Sister instead used her [[lightsaber]] to stab the Grand Inquisitor, mockingly asking him if he thought that she would let him take all the credit, before letting him drop to the ground. ====Reclaiming his title==== {{Quote|Hello, Third Sister. Revenge does wonders for the will to live, don't you think? Your rage was useful. Now it is tiresome. We will leave you where we found you. In the gutter, where you belong. Goodbye… Grand Inquisitor.|The Grand Inquisitor reveals his survival to Reva|{{Kenobi|Part V}}}} Following the purported death of the Pau'an, the Third Sister communicated with Vader via hologram. There, Sevander asserted that Kenobi would pay for the Grand Inquisitor's assumed demise, but Lord Vader responded that the Grand Inquisitor no longer meant anything. He went on to promise her the position of Grand Inquisitor to the Third Sister should she prove herself, though the Fifth Brother, who was next-in-line for the position, contested her claim.{{Kenobi|Part III}} [[File:Grand_Inquisitor_Part_VI.png|thumb|right|250px|The Grand Inquisitor counsels Darth Vader to continue chasing Kawlan Roken's freighter.]] Due to her success in placing a tracker to uncover the location of the Path network and Kenobi, the Third Sister was granted the title of Grand Inquisitor. However, due to his desire for revenge, the Pau'an was able to survive his wound and recover from Sevander's attack. After the Third Sister betrayed Vader during their mission on [[Jabiim]], she was struck down by her former master. As she lay weakened on the ground, the Grand Inquisitor reappeared and revealed his survival to Sevander. He told Sevander, since her rage had become tiresome, the Inquisitorius would abandon her in the gutter. He then took the pin signifying the rank of Grand Inquisitor from her, reclaiming his rank, before he and Vader left Sevander for dead. The Grand Inquisitor and Vader returned to the latter's flagship, the ''[[Devastator]]'', as it pursued [[Kawlan Roken]]'s freighter. In the midst of their pursuit, the Imperials noticed a single drop ship exit the freighter and detected one lifeform aboard. Vader immediately realized that it was Kenobi, but the Grand Inquisitor counseled his master that they continue their pursuit of Roken's ship, opining that they should not prioritize one Jedi. However, Vader countered that Kenobi was no ordinary Jedi, then ordered the ''Devastator'' to pursue Kenobi's ship. As Kenobi reached a rocky moon, Vader asked the [[Unidentified Devastator captain|captain]] to prepare his ship. As Vader walked off the bridge, the Grand Inquisitor eyed him briefly.{{Kenobi|Part VI}} ===Nemesis of the Spectres=== ====The children of the Force==== {{Quote|The Jedi Knights are all but destroyed. And yet your task is not complete, Inquisitor. The Emperor has foreseen a new threat rising against him; the children of the Force. They must not become Jedi.''"
"''Yes, Lord Vader.''"
"''Hunt down this new enemy. And if they will not serve the Empire, eliminate them along with any surviving Jedi who would train them. This is my master's command.''"
"''And so it will be done.|Darth Vader and the Grand Inquisitor|{{Rebels|Spark of Rebellion}}}} In the years prior to the [[Battle of Yavin]], the Grand Inquisitor was contacted by Lord Vader, who told the [[Jedi hunter]] that the Emperor had foreseen a new threat rising to challenge his rule: the "children of the Force," who could not be allowed to become Jedi. Thus, the Inquisitor was instructed to hunt these individuals down and either make them serve the Empire or destroy them, along with any Jedi survivors who could train them. With the orders of the Emperor given, the Inquisitor told his master that it would be done. [[File:Inquisitor_Speaks_to_Vader.png|thumb|left|250px|The Grand Inquisitor was ordered by Darth Vader to hunt down the "children of the Force."]] One method that the Inquisitor used to find Force-sensitive individuals was to look for [[cadet]]s at the [[Academy for Young Imperials]] on [[Lothal]] who met a set of criteria, one that indicated their ability to use the Force,{{Rebels|Breaking Ranks}} an operation known as [[Project Harvester]]. One known target of Project Harvester was [[Dhara Leonis]], a promising cadet and the daughter of Imperial agricultural scientists. The Imperial authorities attempted to cover up her kidnapping by claiming that she had run away from the Academy.''[[Servants of the Empire: Rebel in the Ranks]]'' However, her mother, [[Tepha Leonis|Tepha]], and younger brother [[Zare Leonis]] suspected that the Empire was lying. To ascertain his sister's fate, Zare enrolled at the Academy the following year.''[[Servants of the Empire: Edge of the Galaxy]]'' Sometime later, fourteen years after the rise of the Empire, a group of [[Spectres|rebels]] who operated on Lothal came to the attention of [[Agent]] [[Alexsandr Kallus]] of the [[Imperial Security Bureau]]. The rebels [[Mission to free Wookiee prisoners|rescued]] a group of [[Wookiee]]s that had been [[Slavery|enslaved]] in the [[Spice mines of Kessel|spice mines]] of [[Kessel]], a mission in which the rebel leader, [[Kanan Jarrus]], used a [[lightsaber]] and revealed himself as a Jedi survivor. After the rebels escaped, Kallus contacted the Inquisitor and informed him about what happened on Kessel. The Inquisitor was pleased that Kallus informed him of the rebel cell and the Jedi in its ranks. ====Trap on Stygeon Prime==== {{Quote|Yes, I'm afraid Master Luminara died with the Republic, but her bones continue to serve the Empire. Luring the last Jedi to their ends.|The Grand Inquisitor to Kanan Jarrus and Ezra Bridger|}} The Grand Inquisitor laid a trap for Jarrus and his Padawan, [[Ezra Bridger]], in the Spire. The Empire was able to project an image suggesting that she was alive, and this information was then reported by [[Gall Trayvis]], a former member of the [[Imperial Senate]] who claimed to have gone into exile after speaking out against the Empire—in reality, Trayvis was a loyal agent of the Empire, one who used his position to lure rebel groups into traps around the galaxy.{{Rebels|Vision of Hope}} Not wanting to pass up an opportunity to rescue a Jedi survivor, the rebels undertook a [[Duel on Stygeon Prime|mission]] to the Spire, where they intended to rescue the Jedi Master. [[File:Kanan_vs_Inquisitor.png|thumb|right|250px|The Grand Inquisitor confronted Kanan Jarrus, a Jedi Padawan who survived the execution of Order 66.]] Once in the prison, the rebels fought their way through [[stormtrooper]]s who were stationed there. Jarrus and Bridger made it to the detention area, and Jarrus believed he could sense the Jedi Master—though, in actuality, it was the power from her bones. They entered the cell and saw a projected image of Unduli, which faded into a sarcophagus that revealed the remains of the Jedi Master. The Grand Inquisitor entered the cell, his lightsaber ignited, and approached the two Jedi, revealing that Luminara had been dead for many years. Jarrus attacked the Inquisitor and the two engaged in lightsaber combat. The Inquisitor was able to correctly deduce that Jarrus had been trained by Jedi Master [[Depa Billaba]], as she had been a teacher of [[Form III]] lightsaber combat in close-quarter fighting, which Jarrus employed extensively. The two continued their duel within the cell until Bridger set off a small detonator that allowed him and Jarrus to flee. Though they had escaped the cell, the Grand Inquisitor pursued them and continued his fight with Jarrus in the halls of the prison. He soon pushed Jarrus away through the Force and, per Vader's command, attempted to convert Bridger to the dark side. The boy refused, however, and the Inquisitor prepared to strike him down, but Jarrus used the Force to pin the Inquisitor to the ceiling, giving the two Jedi a chance to flee. The Grand Inquisitor followed them and chased them through the prison before they met back up with their fellow rebels. Separated by a number of closed doors, the Inquisitor sliced through them with his lightsaber and arrived in time to see the rebels beginning to escape. He made one last attempt to stop them by throwing his lightsaber towards them, but Jarrus deflected it and the rebels escaped aboard the ''[[Phantom]]'', the attack shuttle that belonged to their main ship, the ''[[Ghost]]''. ====Incident at the Imperial Academy==== {{Quote|Well, Leonis, let's take a walk, shall we? I want to know everything about your ''former'' friends.|The Grand Inquisitor, to Zare Leonis|}} [[File:The_Grand_Inquisitor_and_Zare_Leonis.png|thumb|left|250px|Zare Leonis suspected that the Grand Inquisitor was involved in the disappearance of his sister, Dhara Leonis.]] After his failure to stop the rebels on Stygeon Prime, the Inquisitor was contacted by [[Commandant]] [[Cumberlayne Aresko]], the lead officer at the Imperial Academy on Lothal, who informed him of two students who potentially met his criteria for Force-sensitivity. He learned that these cadets were Dev Morgan—who, unknown to the Academy, was Bridger in disguise, who [[Mission to destroy a kyber crystal|infiltrated]] the Academy to learn the location of a giant [[kyber crystal]] of great power—and [[Jai Kell]]. Having learned this information, the Inquisitor, speaking via hologram, told Aresko that he would arrive at the Imperial Academy the next day. Bridger overheard the conversation, and he and Kell escaped the Academy with another cadet, Zare Leonis, who suspected that the Inquisitor was behind the disappearance of his sister, Dhara Leonis; Dhara was the star cadet at the Academy before her disappearance, which the Empire claimed was a result of her running away from the Academy. Upon his arrival at the Imperial Academy, Aresko and Agent Kallus informed him of Bridger and Kell's escape. The Jedi hunter was shown the data files on the two cadets and recognized "Dev Morgan" as Bridger from their encounter on Stygeon Prime. The Inquisitor informed Aresko that the incident was a black mark on the Academy's record, though he did have hope of learning more about the rebels, as Leonis was also present in the meeting. During the escape, Leonis had opted to stay behind so he could find out what happened to his sister and pretended to try to stop Bridger and Kell upon their escape. The Inquisitor spoke to Leonis and told the cadet to tell him everything he knew about Bridger and Kell. During his private chat with Leonis, the Inquisitor led the young cadet to an interrogation room. Once inside, the Inquisitor asked Leonis everything he knew about Morgan while trying to probe the cadet's thoughts. While hiding his collaboration with Morgan, Leonis pretended to support the Inquisitor's assessment that something was not right about Morgan. When the Inquisitor told Leonis that Morgan was a pseudonym, Zare pretended to be a "perfect cadet" and asked whether the victories in his assessments would be vacated. The Inquisitor merely replied that he should ask Commandant Aresko. Zare then attempted to convince the Inquisitor that he was Force-sensitive like his missing sister Dhara. He claimed that he could somehow sense that there was something wrong with Dev and Jai and that they were hiding something. The Inquisitor quickly deduced that Leonis was Dhara's younger brother. While the Inquisitor was fully aware that Dhara had been abducted and forcibly inducted into Project Harvester, he repeated the official Imperial account that Dhara had merely run away. When Zare claimed that he and his sister could always sense each others' presence, the Inquisitor merely told the young cadet that it made sense and that in time he would understand why. ====Skirmish on Vyndal==== {{Quote|Another Jedi! This is indeed a surprise. How many more Padawans have you taken?"
"He's not my Padawan."
"Then you won't be emotionally compromised when he dies.|The Grand Inquisitor, to Kanan Jarrus about Yeleb the Protector|{{RebelsMagCite|3|The Fake Jedi}}}} The Inquisitor and his Imperial forces arrived in a [[Unidentified village (Vyndal)|village]] on the planet [[Vyndal]] in search of Jarrus after he had been seen close by. The Inquisitor and his forces were greeted by the protector of the village, [[Yeleb]], who lied to the Inquisitor that he had not seen Jarrus in their village; however, the Inquisitor could see through the protector's lies, and when Yeleb ordered the Imperials to leave, the Pau'an ordered his stormtroopers to destroy the village. [[File:Skirmish_on_Vyndal.png|thumb|right|250px|The Grand Inquisitor killed Yeleb, but failed to capture Kanan Jarrus on Vyndal.]] Jarrus revealed himself to the Inquisitor and [[Skirmish on Vyndal|attacked]] him. Yeleb would soon join the combat as well, wielding his own green-bladed lightsaber, leading the Inquisitor to assume that Yeleb was a Jedi too, although, in actual fact, a few years earlier Yeleb had taken the lightsaber from a crashed [[Eta-2 Actis-class light interceptor|Eta-2 ''Actis''-class light interceptor]] with a dead [[Unidentified Jedi (Vyndal)|Jedi]] [[pilot]] inside. Using the Force, the Inquisitor pushed Jarrus out of combat, allowing him to focus on Yeleb and slash the man across the chest with his blade. After Yeleb collapsed onto the floor, the Inquisitor took Yeleb's lightsaber and Jarrus fled from the Inquisitor to draw him away from the wounded [[human]]. The Pau'an along with his stormtroopers gave chase, and Jarrus was able to trick the Imperials into thinking he had fled Vyndal on one of their [[cruiser]]s, causing them to chase after it and leave the planet in the other. After the Imperials left the planet, Yeleb died of his injuries, and Jarrus ended up leaving the planet and returning to the rebels, leaving the [[Unidentified Vyndal species|people of Vyndal]] with hope that without him and the lightsaber on the planet, the Empire would not return, and even if they did, the people were able to protect themselves. ====Empire Day==== {{Quote|I still sense the Jedi and his Padawan, within my ''grasp''.|The Grand Inquisitor|}} The Inquisitor was on Lothal for [[Empire Day]] when the rebels destroyed the prototype [[TIE/ad v1]]. When the rebels attempted to smuggle [[Tseebo]], an [[Imperial Information Office]] worker who had fled with Imperial secrets, off Lothal, he led a TIE fighter squadron while piloting his own [[The Inquisitor's TIE Advanced|TIE/ad v1]] to stop them from escaping. He was able to plant an [[XX-23 S-thread tracker]] on their ship moments before they jumped to hyperspace.{{Rebels|Empire Day (episode)}} [[File:The_Grand_Inquisitor_on_Fort_Anaxes.png|thumb|left|250px|The Grand Inquisitor tracked Jarrus and his apprentice, Ezra Bridger, to the ruins of Fort Anaxes.]] Realizing they were being tracked, Jarrus and Bridger boarded the ''Phantom'' and ejected from the ''Ghost'', flying it to [[Fort Anaxes]]. The Inquisitor took a squad of troops and its [[Unidentified stormtrooper commander (PM-1203)|commander]] with him aboard a [[Sentinel-class landing craft|''Sentinel''-class landing craft]] to confront the two Jedi. As the Inquisitor and his troopers entered the base, they spotted Jarrus and Bridger along with a multitude of [[fyrnock]]s. The two Jedi used the Force to command the fyrnocks to attack the stormtroopers. Jarrus fought the Inquisitor once more, but he was easily overwhelmed and knocked out. Cornering Bridger, the Inquisitor told him to give in to the dark side, and that his friends would die and that everything he fought for would be lost. Bridger briefly succumbed to the dark side and summoned a giant fyrnock to attack the Inquisitor. Jarrus reawakened, grabbing Bridger and reclaiming his lightsaber. After driving off the mother fyrnock, the Inquisitor attempted to halt their escape, but they managed to board their ship, the ''Phantom'', and destroy the Imperial landing craft. Accepting his failure, the Inquisitor simply stated that his [[Anakin Skywalker|master]] would not be pleased. ====Dealing with Zare Leonis==== {{Quote|Who can doubt the commitment of such a promising young cadet?|The Grand Inquisitor probing Zare Leonis|''[[Servants of the Empire: Imperial Justice]]''}} [[File:Morgan_and_Leonis_Secret_Meeting.jpg|thumb|right|250px|The Grand Inquisitor suspected that Zare Leonis had secret ties to Ezra Bridger and his Lothal-based rebel cell.]] Following the Lothal rebels' attack on the Empire Day celebrations, the Grand Inquisitor returned to Lothal to deal with another unfinished business: Dhara Leonis' younger brother Zare Leonis. While Zare was a promising cadet at the Academy for Young Imperials who had earned the glowing praise of his instructors, the Inquisitor suspected that Leonis was connected to Ezra Bridger and the other Lothal rebels. A perfect opportunity to make his move against Zare surfaced when the young cadet took action against an unscrupulous fellow cadet named [[Nazhros Oleg]], who had attempted to shield his smuggler uncles from Imperial justice. Under the pretext of rewarding Leonis, the Inquisitor arranged for the cadet to be transferred to the [[Arkanis Academy]], which was connected to Project Harvester. There, he hoped to create the circumstances that would expose Leonis as a traitor to the Empire. In addition, the Inquisitor wanted to ascertain whether Zare was actually Force-sensitive as he had claimed earlier. Following Leonis' raid on a group of smugglers, the Inquisitor and [[Captain]] [[Piers Roddance]] summoned Zare for a private meeting. When Leonis suggested that Oleg was genuinely unaware that his uncles were involved in smuggling and suggested showing the delinquent some compassion, the Inquisitor replied that compassion was the most insidious business. After ordering Captain Roddance to leave the room, the Inquisitor told Leonis that he had arranged for the cadet to be transferred to the Arkanis Academy as a "reward" for his loyalty to the Empire. Throughout the meeting, the Inquisitor made every effort to probe Leonis' thoughts. Pretending to be a "model" cadet, Leonis expressed gratitude at the opportunity to serve the Empire. Sensing Leonis' true motivations for joining the Imperial Academy, the Inquisitor patronized Leonis by asking "who could doubt the commitment of such a promising young cadet." Intimidated by the Inquisitor, Leonis turned away from the Pau'an's gaze, prompting the Inquisitor to ask the cadet to make eye contact with him. Prior to Leonis' departure, the Inquisitor told the cadet that he looked forward to his training on Arkanis and "assured" the Cadet that his service to the Empire would be more important than he had hoped for. While Leonis was uncertain whether the Inquisitor knew his true agenda, his girlfriend [[Merei Spanjaf]] uncovered Imperial documents which confirmed that the Inquisitor had intended to use the Arkanis transfer to break the young cadet. Later, the Inquisitor visited the Arkanis Academy and landed at [[Area Null]], a secluded tower in the Academy that hosted several top-secret Imperial projects including Project Harvester and [[Project Unity]], the latter a program for re-educating former dissident youths. After dining with Commandant [[Brendol Hux]] and the cadets in the Academy's banquet hall, the Inquisitor summoned Cadet Leonis for a private meeting at the Commandant's balcony. There, the Inquisitor asked Leonis why he had tried to enter Area Null even though it was off-limits to Cadets. Leonis claimed that he thought that a fellow cadet was in trouble but the Inquisitor quickly realized that he was lying.''[[Servants of the Empire: The Secret Academy]]'' He then gave Leonis a second chance to answer his question. Leonis claimed that he had sensed that there was something in that tower that he was meant to find. The Inquisitor then asked if Morgan had told him about the tower on Lothal or something called Project Harvester. In response, Leonis feigned ignorance but the Inquisitor could see that he was trying to hide something. Before the Inquisitor could carry on with the interrogation, the Commandant's droid [[DDM-38]] arrived and informed him that he had received a priority encrypted message from Lothal. Before leaving, the Inquisitor warned Leonis that he would soon have Morgan and his companions. He also vowed to get to the truth behind Leonis' connection to Morgan. Unknown to the Inquisitor and Leonis, this was to be their last meeting due to unexpected developments. ====Talking with Rae Sloane==== {{Quote|Vice Admiral…''"
"''Not now, I-- *gasp*''"
"''Vice Admiral Rae Sloane, I am the ''Emperor's Grand Inquisitor''… and I want you to tell me ''everything'' you know… about your ''hobby''.|The Grand Inquisitor and Rae Sloane|[[Kanan 12|''Kanan'' 12]]}} To continue tracking the rebels, at some point the Grand Inquisitor sought information from [[Vice Admiral]] [[Rae Sloane]] of the [[Imperial Navy]]. Sloane once had a run-in with Jarrus on the planet [[Gorse]], where Jarrus first met Captain [[Hera Syndulla]] and joined her rebel cause.[[A New Dawn (novel)|''A New Dawn'']] The Grand Inquisitor found the [[officer]] on [[Lahn]], where she had set a trap for the Jedi. Jarrus escaped, but Sloane remained on Lahn when she was confronted by the Inquisitor—who wanted to know everything she knew about Jarrus. ====Visions of darkness==== {{Quote|Ready to die, boy, or are you afraid to face your demise?''"
"''No. Afraid of being alone again? Sure. Afraid of letting down my master? Absolutely.''"
"''Your master lies dead and rotting in a forgotten tunnel. You could hardly have let him down more.''"
"''I'm not afraid.|The vision of the Grand Inquisitor speaks to Ezra Bridger|{{Rebels|Path of the Jedi}}}} [[File:Vision_of_the_Inquisitor.png|thumb|left|250px|In the Jedi Temple on Lothal, the vision of the Grand Inquisitor represented Bridger's fears.]] Having had his first experience with the dark side on Fort Anaxes, Bridger ventured to the [[Lothal Jedi Temple|Jedi Temple]] on Lothal with Jarrus, who wanted to make sure that his Padawan could actually become a Jedi. Once inside the temple, Bridger encountered visions of the Grand Inquisitor killing his friends, whom he had come to regard as his family. The Inquisitor first dueled and killed Jarrus in the vision, before entering the ''Ghost'' and killing the crew inside. Soon thereafter, the vision of the Grand Inquisitor moved to kill Bridger himself. Bridger realized, however, that he was not afraid of dying. Rather, he was afraid of losing those he cared about and being abandoned like he was when he lost his parents at a young age—a fear represented through the threat of the Inquisitor. Once Bridger realized what his fear was, the vision of the Grand Inquisitor disappeared. ====Capturing Kanan==== {{Quote|Inquisitor, I am giving you the opportunity to redeem yourself. Do not disappoint me, and remember, I want this Jedi, alive.''"
"''Your faith will be rewarded.|Grand Moff Tarkin and the Grand Inquisitor|{{Rebels|Call to Action}}}} The Inquisitor was present in the Imperial Complex hangar when [[Grand Moff]] [[Wilhuff Tarkin]] arrived to investigate the situation on Lothal. Reports of the rebel activities had reached the highest levels of the Imperial government and worries had begun to emerge as Lothal's industries were vital for the Empire's expansion into the [[Outer Rim Territories|Outer Rim]]. Immediately upon arriving, [[Governor]] Tarkin berated [[Minister]] [[Maketh Tua]] and Agent Kallus for their inability to stop the rebellion. He also dismissed the rumors that a Jedi was leading the rebels, claiming that all the Jedi had died during the Purge and that he knew because he had witnessed it. Later that day, Governor Tarkin summoned Commandant Cumberlayne Aresko and [[Taskmaster]] [[Myles Grint]] who had been pursuing the rebels for some time and who had failed at every turn. After a brief conversation during which he revealed that other rebel cells were active in the Empire and that the rumors of a Jedi leading a rebellion could spark hope and encourage unity, the Grand Moff informed the assembled dignitaries that there would be consequences for failure henceforth. Upon these words, the Inquisitor activated his lightsaber directly behind Aresko and Grint and triggered the spinning feature, decapitating the two officers as a horrified Tua and Kallus watched on. When Kallus discovered that the Rebels were planning to strike at the Imperial communications tower, Tarkin instructed him to let them enter the tower but prepare his troops to intervene as soon as they did. After the Agent left, the Grand Moff told the Grand Inquisitor that this was his chance to redeem himself for his previous failures. The Pau'an promised Tarkin that his faith would be rewarded. [[File:GrandInquisitorVsJarrus-CallToAction.png|thumb|right|250px|The Grand Inquisitor and Jarrus dueled outside the communication tower.]] After the Rebels struck the tower, Kallus and his troops intervened, surrounding the tower and forcing the Rebels to escape to the roof. Only Kanan Jarrus remained behind to give them time to escape, at which point the Inquisitor arrived to confront the Jedi. Jarrus destroyed the console giving them access to the tower. Once again, the Inquisitor and the Jedi fought, with the former noticing that Jarrus had improved his technique. However, the Inquisitor proved the stronger of the two once again and he subdued Jarrus with the Force. However, the rest of the Rebels escaped. With Jarrus in custody, Governor Tarkin arrived and was given the captured Jedi just as a signal broadcast by the rebels begun to transmit by the tower. The Grand Moff gave orders for the tower to be destroyed before leaving with his prisoner. ====Kanan's interrogation==== {{Quote|Tell me, Jedi, how did you survive Order 66? It was your master Billaba who laid down her life for yours. Do you remember her last words to you? Her last and final breath before she died? You do, don't you? You see it in your sleep, you hear her voice when you wake. Tell me, Jedi. What was her last word to you?''"
"''Run''.|The Grand Inquisitor asks Jarrus about his master's last words|}} [[File:Inquisitor-tortures-Kanan.png|thumb|left|250px|Despite capturing Jarrus, the Grand Inquisitor was unable to probe the Jedi's mind with the Force.]] After Jarrus was captured, he was brought aboard Governor Tarkin's [[flagship]] in orbit above Lothal: the ''[[Sovereign]]''. Tarkin and Kallus proceed to interrogate Jarrus with a [[mind probe]] but the Jedi proved stronger than this tactic. As the Grand Moff grew more frustrated with the lack of results, the Inquisitor arrived and told them that Jedi were trained to resist mind probes. Instead, he claimed that pain would be a more effective technique, as Jedi still felt it. The Inquisitor used the Force to try and pry the information from Jarrus' mind but, once again, the Jedi resisted. Instead, the Inquisitor electrocuted Jarrus to make him talk. However, the rebel proved to be far stronger than he believed, and he resisted the torture. The Inquisitor came to believe that Jarrus did not know anything of a larger rebellion. Tarkin eventually suggested transferring him to a [[Fortress Vader|facility]] that had never failed to gain results. The ''Sovereign'' then departed Lothal for [[Mustafar]], a world deep in the Outer Rim.{{Rebels|Rebel Resolve}} [[File:TarkinAndGrandInquisitor-SWRS01E14.jpg|thumb|right|250px|Wilhuff Tarkin observed the Grand Inquisitor's interrogation of Jarrus.]] Over Mustafar, the Inquisitor continued his interrogation of Jarrus, asking him about other rebels he may have known. Specifically, he wanted to know about a mysterious rebel known as "Fulcrum." Jarrus still refused to talk, so the Inquisitor changed tactics: he asked Jarrus how he had survived Order 66. When Jarrus failed to answer, the Inquisitor revealed that he knew how; Jarrus' Master, Depa Billaba, had sacrificed herself to save him, losing her own life in the process. The Inquisitor taunted Jarrus, asking him if he remembered his Master's last words, and Jarrus answered that she told him to run. The Inquisitor told Jarrus that he could not save his friends any more than he could save his Master because he feared his own power and did not even dare wear his lightsaber in public because of it. When alarms went off, the Inquisitor was unsurprised to find that the other rebels had come to [[Action at Mustafar|rescue]] their friend. ====Confrontation aboard the ''Sovereign''==== {{Quote|You have no idea what you've unleashed here today. There are some things far more frightening than death.|The Grand Inquisitor to Kanan Jarrus, immediately before committing suicide|}} After Bridger broke Jarrus out of his cell, they headed back for their evacuation ship through the generator complex. The Inquisitor waited for them and ignited his lightsaber. Jarrus borrowed [[Ezra Bridger's first lightsaber|Bridger's lightsaber]] and attacked the Inquisitor. As he was about to reach him, he activated the lightsaber's stun gun, surprising his opponent. The two engaged in a lightsaber duel with Jarrus using both the blade and the stun gun to attack the Inquisitor. When Bridger used the Force to snatch Jarrus' lightsaber from the Imperial agent's belt, the Inquisitor disengaged from the duel with Jarrus and, activating his second blade, claimed that he would finally get the challenge that he had always wanted. After a brief engagement, he used the Force to push Jarrus back before throwing his spinning lightsaber at Bridger, who fell from the pathway, to Jarrus' horror. Distraught at the apparent loss of his Padawan, Jarrus remained on his knees for a while as the Inquisitor stood over him, smiling sadistically at the Jedi's obvious anguish. However, he eventually pulled himself together, remembering his Jedi training, and rose to his feet. When the Inquisitor asked him what would happen now that no one else would die for him, Jarrus replied that he no longer had anything left to fear. He then used the Force to draw his lightsaber to him, using both it and Ezra's. After saluting each other, the Inquisitor and the Jedi resumed their duel. [[File:InquisitorDeath.png|thumb|left|250px|Unwilling to face his master's wrath, the Grand Inquisitor allowed himself to fall into the ''Sovereign''{{'s}} exploding reactor.]] This time, however, Jarrus proved a much more effective foe, and he gradually started to drive the Inquisitor back, the latter of whom began to show fear and uncertainty for the first time. When the Inquisitor came perilously close to the edge, Jarrus interrupted the duel to say that his foe was right: he was a coward but that he had discovered that there was something far more powerful than fear: the Force. The Inquisitor made his blades spin to defend himself, but Jarrus destroyed the Inquisitor's lightsaber and the Imperial agent fell off the edge, catching the side of the pathway in his fall. The two halves of his lightsaber hit the generator, causing it to catch fire and starting a chain reaction within the ''Sovereign''. As the Jedi stood over his defeated foe, the Inquisitor looked up and told Jarrus that his defeat would unleash something far worse upon them all. Knowing the punishment he would receive from his master for his failure, the Inquisitor said that there were some things far more frightening than death before letting himself fall into the exploding generator, killing himself. ===Post-mortem=== ====Master Yoda's emissary==== {{Quote|The temple is falling. Go. I will delay the enemy.|The Sentinel, to Kanan Jarrus|}} The Inquisitor's warning to Jarrus proved true. With their primary agent on Lothal dead and a growing rebellion in the galaxy, the Empire sent out a far deadlier agent to Lothal to root out and destroy the rebels: Darth Vader. After the Dark Lord [[Attack on Phoenix Squadron (4 BBY)|attacked]] and crippled [[Phoenix Cell]] and learned that his former Padawan, Ahsoka Tano, was still alive and in league with the rebellion, Sidious ordered Vader to dispatch another Inquisitor to hunt the rebels.{{Rebels|The Siege of Lothal}} The latter sent the Seventh Sister and the Fifth Brother, both of whom hoped to become the new Grand Inquisitor. [[File:Kanan_vs_the_Sentinel.png|thumb|right|250px|Jarrus experienced a vision of the Grand Inquisitor as he once was, a Knight of the Jedi Order.]] Sometime after the death of the Grand Inquisitor, Jarrus and Bridger traveled with Ahsoka Tano to the Jedi Temple on Lothal to seek the guidance of Jedi Master [[Yoda]], with whom Jarrus and Bridger had communed with from there before. It was there that they hoped to find guidance for how to deal with the threat of the Inquisitors, who attacked the rebels at every turn. While in the temple, Jarrus entered a vision in which he saw a Jedi Temple Guard known as the Sentinel within a dojo. Unknown to Jarrus, this was a vision conjured by Yoda of the Grand Inquisitor, as the Jedi he once was.{{RebelsRecon|VM4PSIlIrl4|#2.17: Inside "Shroud of Darkness" | Star Wars Rebels|sw_url=video/rebels-recon-inside-shroud-of-darkness}} The Sentinel warned Jarrus that Bridger would fall to the dark side of the Force and that the boy had to be eliminated. Jarrus refused and the two engaged in a lightsaber duel. By the end of the duel, Jarrus refused to fight any further and admitted that while he may not be able to protect Bridger forever, he would continue to do his best to train him. The Sentinel looked as if he was about to strike Jarrus down but instead performed the knighting ritual. Then he removed his mask to reveal the face of the Grand Inquisitor. Jarrus asked what everything that had happened meant, and the Sentinel said that it meant Jarrus was now a Jedi Knight, as the Grand Inquisitor once was. As the Seventh Sister and the Fifth Brother descended on the temple, the Sentinel told Jarrus to flee and said he would hold off the enemy. The vision of the Sentinel, flanked by other Jedi Temple Guards, surrounded the two Inquisitors as Jarrus, Bridger, and Tano fled from the Jedi Temple. In [[1 BBY]], shortly after Jarrus' own death, his confrontation with the Grand Inquisitor was heard among numerous voices by Bridger as he passed through a [[Hyperspace tunneling|hyper tunnel]] while riding a [[Loth-wolf]] on his [[mission to the Lothal Jedi Temple]].{{Rebels|Wolves and a Door}} ====Eternal pawn of the Sith==== {{Quote|I have served…for so long. Will there never…be a chance…of release?''"
"''You are but a tool, shaped to serve my purposes. You will…continue.|The Inquisitor's spirit and Darth Vader|}} [[File:GrandInquisitorGhost-2020StarWars6.jpg|thumb|left|250px|An abandoned Jedi outpost on Tempes was haunted by the spirit of the Grand Inquisitor.]] Despite his defeat above Mustafar, the Pau'an's usefulness to the Sith had not run dry. Through the intervention of Vader, the Grand Inquisitor was prevented from passing on from the mortal world; instead, Vader forced the Inquisitor's spirit to serve his purposes. The Dark Lord installed his servant into a [[High Republic Era]] [[Jedi outpost (Tempes)|Jedi outpost]] on [[Tempes]], hoping that anyone seeking knowledge from the place would be caught in his trap. The Inquisitor's spirit, still burning from the flames his body had been destroyed in aboard the ''Sovereign'', haunted the structure for years, killing any seekers of knowledge who stepped foot into its halls. At some point, the partially trained Padawan [[Verla]] discovered the outpost, but abandoned the place after sensing the dark presence of the Inquisitor that resided within. After losing [[Skywalker lightsaber|his lightsaber]] in a [[Duel on Cloud City|duel]] with Vader on [[Cloud City]] in [[3 ABY]], the aspiring Jedi [[Luke Skywalker]] learned of the Tempes outpost from Verla and traveled there, hoping to retrieve a new weapon. Inside, the Inquisitor's spirit confronted the boy and taunted him for his lack of training. Armed with the lightsaber of a Jedi Temple Guard, Skywalker battled the spirit. The ghostly Inquisitor gained the upper hand in the duel, knocking the would-be Jedi to the ground and mocking him for his devotion to the Jedi Order. Although the dark side adept sneered that the Force did not save the Order from extinction, the sight of ancient [[Jedi artifact|relics]] in the outpost, still standing after [[Standard century|centuries]], motivated Skywalker to push back. The aspiring Jedi recognized that service to a greater good was worth dying for, and, with his new weapon, sliced off the spirit's hand and delivered a slash to his chest, causing the Inquisitor to disappear.
